observation: Arrayy\create($data) was typed @param mixed with a fixed @return Arrayy<int|string,mixed,array<int|string,mixed>>, so array inputs lost their key and value types. A function-level template bound to the mixed parameter with a conditional @phpstan-return recovered them: Arrayy<(T is array<array-key,mixed> ? key-of<T> : int|string),(T is array<array-key,mixed> ? value-of<T> : mixed),(T is array<array-key,mixed> ? T : array<int|string,mixed>)>. Map, list and array-shape inputs kept precise types; Traversable, callable, scalar, null and object inputs kept the old fallback; mixed collapsed to an equivalent type. The inner @var cast had to restate the same conditional type to satisfy return.type.

evidence.summary: voku/Arrayy PR #195 (head 0e6c394): tests/PHPStan/CreateFactoryInference.php fails 11 ways on base de7df89 (including the legacy Arrayy<int,string> consumer) and passes with the change; PHPUnit 1391 tests, PHPStan level 8, Legacy fixture and negative fixture unchanged; CI green on PHP 8.0-8.5 and Infection on the exact head.

hypothesis: When a PHP factory must keep accepting every runtime input, a union such as array<K,V>|mixed collapses to mixed and swallows the template, whereas binding the whole parameter to a template and branching in the return type keeps array inputs precise without narrowing accepted inputs.
validated_conclusion: For typed-factory inference on a PHPStan version that supports conditional return types over templates, prefer a template on the whole parameter plus a conditional @phpstan-return with key-of/value-of over narrowing @phpstan-param or overloads; keep the native @return as the documented fallback, restate the conditional in the body @var, prove it with an assertType fixture that is red on the base commit and green on the change, and include a legacy two-template consumer in that fixture. Callable-typed method fixtures must give an optional key parameter when the signature declares one optional.
